title: Trading Costs, Liquidity, and Liquidity Risk
source: Lecture10_MGT595_2025.pptx (144 slides; several charts have embedded real data)
papers: Frazzini, Israel & Moskowitz, 'Trading Costs of Asset Pricing Anomalies' (AQR $1.7T live-trade database)
Acharya & Pedersen (2005) liquidity-adjusted CAPM; Pastor & Stambaugh (2003)
Brunnermeier & Pedersen (2009) liquidity spirals; Mitchell, Pedersen & Pulvino (2007)

page_groups.content: Outline: trading costs (implementation shortfall, adjusting backtests), portfolio implementation, liquidity (definitions, effect on prices), liquidity risk. Sources of illiquidity: exogenous transaction costs (fees, taxes); demand pressure/search; inventory risk (compensate market maker for price risk); private information (adverse selection, fundamentals or order flow); locating a counterparty (OTC search frictions). Both liquidity LEVEL and liquidity RISK are theoretically priced.

IMPLEMENTATION SHORTFALL (Perold): paper portfolio = wish portfolio at mid-quotes with unlimited size; Shortfall = paper return - real return = EXECUTION COSTS + OPPORTUNITY COSTS (paper profit on trades not done / limit orders never hit). Trade fast: high TC, low opportunity cost; trade slow: reverse. Manage effort: low shortfall -> improve strategies; high-TC shortfall -> trade slower; high-opportunity shortfall -> trade faster. E(TC) = f(order size, speed, volume, volatility, shares out, float, date...). Backtest adjustment: each rebalance compute implied trades, subtract E(TC), recompute Sharpe.

Measures menu (image: spreads, Amihud, etc.). Trading cost over the century (Jones): costs at record lows, turnover up (54% to 99% daily 1994-2004). Korajczyk-Sadka (2004) TAQ estimates for momentum: proportional costs for extreme winners (REAL table): effective spread cost 0.19%/mo EW, 0.12 VW; quoted spread 0.26 EW, 0.17 VW; plus price impact rising in size -> small break-even fund sizes; Lee-Ready signing; Kyle linear theory, empirically slightly concave. CAVEATS: assumes demanding liquidity all at once, average TAQ trade, naive strategy; patience and supplying liquidity can cut costs a lot at the price of tracking error. Re-optimize on E(r)-E(TC).

FRAZZINI-ISRAEL-MOSKOWITZ live-trade database: ALL longer-term equity orders of AQR 1998-2016, $1.7 TRILLION traded, ~9,543 stocks, 21 developed markets, automated algorithms, HF trades excluded; orders broken up, randomized, LIQUIDITY-PROVIDING limit orders. HEADLINE: actual costs are ~1/10 of literature estimates. Why: (1) average trade cost != cost facing a patient arbitrageur; (2) passive execution. MI ANATOMY (slide 35 REAL example): average market impact 11 bps = PERMANENT 8.5 + TEMPORARY 2.5 around execution period; pre-execution impact, execution prices, reversal after completion. MI by fraction of daily volume: concave. Tcost model regressions on market returns, size, volatility, trade size; used to predict costs for all stocks. Time variation (spikes in crises). Comparison: Korajczyk-Sadka model predicts far larger costs than realized AQR costs at the same sizes.

ANOMALY NET RETURNS: using actual dollars traded and realized costs - Size, Value, Momentum ALL SURVIVE trading costs at high capacity; SHORT-TERM REVERSAL DOES NOT. Break-even fund sizes (capacities) many times larger than literature claims. Optimized portfolios: minimize costs subject to tracking error to paper factor (SMB/HML/UMD): tracking-error frontier lets net Sharpe and capacity rise substantially - portfolios should be built net of E(TC).

Trade data anatomy: order size known, %DTV unknown; duration is the choice variable. Trade size histogram (REAL): 0-0.5% DTV 1,405,055 orders; 0.5-1% 236,618; 1-1.5% 121,911 ... 4.5-5% 13,776 - overwhelmingly small participation. Duration peaks 6-7 hours (1,268,644). PERMANENT vs TEMPORARY (slide 77 REAL curve data, bps at %DTV): total 2.46 (0), 9.23 (1%), 12.23 (2%), 14.60 (3%), 16.66 (4%), 18.51 (5%); permanent 2.25, 4.06, 5.99, 7.95, 9.91, 11.88 - LINEAR (cannot reject); temporary 0.21, 6.90, 8.61, 9.51, 9.98, 10.19 - CONCAVE (sqrt, log-log coeff 0.49, reject linear). WHY CONCAVE: ENDOGENEITY - patient on trades expected to be expensive; only cheap large trades executed fast. Tests: aggressive trades (75th pct aggressiveness) show LINEAR MI, passive show sqrt; NEW INFLOWS (exogenous size, REAL curves): inflow MI 2.59 (0) to 25.70 bps (5% DTV) vs non-inflow 1.17 to 20.83 - inflows linear (sqrt term insignificant), steeper; with stock+day FE, inflows face a LINEAR function. Lesson: the sqrt cost function everyone estimates is partly an artifact of discretionary trading; the true constraint is closer to linear for forced trades.

Liquidity and PRICES (level): LOOP violations liquidity explains: 3Com/Palm (Lecture 3 callback), on-the-run vs off-the-run Treasuries, restricted shares, put-call parity under shorting constraints. Amihud-style pricing: price = PV(cash flows) - PV(expected trading costs at trading frequency mu); equivalently E(R) = rf + risk premium + mu x c (per-period percentage cost). CLIENTELE effect: short-horizon investors avoid illiquid assets; PATIENT investors hold them and earn MORE than their own amortized costs - liquidity premium exceeds costs of the marginal patient holder; without borrowing constraints this unravels (funding liquidity is what makes market liquidity matter).

LIQUIDITY RISK: definitions - market liquidity (ease of trading) vs market liquidity RISK (costs rise when you need to trade); funding liquidity (trader capital/margins) vs funding liquidity RISK (forced unwind). LIQUIDITY-ADJUSTED CAPM (Acharya-Pedersen, REAL formulas): CAPM holds for NET returns E(R-c) = rf + beta E(Rm-cm-rf), beta = cov(R-c, Rm-cm)/var(Rm-cm). Gross: E(R) = rf + E(c) + [b(R,Rm) + b(c,cm) - b(R,cm) - b(c,Rm)] x premium. FOUR betas: +cov(Ri,Rm) standard; +cov(ci,cm) COMMONALITY in liquidity (bad: your costs rise when everyone's do); -cov(Ri,cm) return sensitivity to aggregate liquidity (assets that PAY OFF when market is illiquid are good); -cov(ci,Rm) liquidity sensitivity to market conditions (assets CHEAP TO SELL in downturns are good). Funding drives market liquidity: speculators need capital W and margins m; feedback both ways -> LIQUIDITY SPIRALS (BP 2009): initial losses -> reduced positions -> prices move away from fundamentals -> further losses (loss spiral) + higher margins (margin spiral) + tighter risk management (risk-management spiral).

RUN FOR THE EXIT price path (theory): prices decline more smoothly than a random walk, SUDDENLY REBOUND (the signature vs fundamentals), end LOWER than start (some investors left). CASES: Quant event Aug 2007 (value-momentum portfolio hammered in the world's most liquid stocks; invisible except through a long/short lens); Convertible bond crisis 2005 (redemptions -> forced sales -> cheapening -> more redemptions; Mitchell-Pedersen-Pulvino); Flash crash May 6 2010 (2-3PM); GFC spillover chain: subprime -> US quant equity -> global quant -> currencies. PRICING: Acharya-Pedersen calibration: liquidity RISK premium 1.1%/yr + liquidity LEVEL premium 3.5%/yr; Pastor-Stambaugh larger (no level control); Bekaert-Harvey-Lundblad emerging markets: LOCAL liquidity risk priced at 85 bp/MONTH, global much smaller. Funding-liquidity measures: TED, on/off-run spread, VIX, quantity measures, PS/AP factors. Conclusions: costs matter for security choice, trade decision, speed, effort; liquidity level AND liquidity risk affect prices.

gap_analysis: The perm/temp MI curves, inflow/non-inflow curves, trade-size and duration histograms are EMBEDDED CHART DATA used exactly.
The 11 = 8.5 + 2.5 bps MI anatomy is the deck's own worked example (slide 35 text).

FIM anomaly net-return and capacity tables are images; the app states the deck's text conclusions (survive: size/value/momentum; fail: STR; costs ~1/10 of literature) without inventing dollar capacities.

The 'Various measures' menu slide is an image; the app lists the standard measures it names generically (spreads, Amihud price-impact ratio, Pastor-Stambaugh reversal, Roll) and keeps formulas to those the deck states (effective/quoted spread definitions appear as headers; the app defines them conventionally and flags that).
Acharya-Pedersen premia (1.1%/3.5%), Bekaert 85bp/mo, and the four-beta decomposition with signs are verbatim deck text.
